record.paper_title: A survey of equivariant map algebras with open problems
record.original_question: Let M be an equivariant map algebra M(X,g)^Γ, formed from an affine scheme X, a target algebra g, and a compatible Γ-action. Extend the theory of global and local Weyl modules from the currently understood cases to more general equivariant map algebras. This includes determining lengths, dimensions, and characters of local Weyl modules, and extending BGG reciprocity to this broader equivariant map algebra setting.

evidence.quote: The action of Γ on X induces an action on the coordinate ring A of X. Then M = (a ⊗ A)Γ , the fixed points of the diagonal action of Γ on a ⊗ A.

(b) Weyl modules. The study of (global and local) Weyl modules for EMAs is an active area of research. In particular, one would like to extend the results on the lengths, dimensions and characters of the local Weyl modules (see [CP01, BN04, CL06, CM04, FL07, Nak01, Nao12]) to the setting of more arbitrary EMAs (see [FMSa] for the definitions of global and local Weyl modules in this setting). It is also natural to try to extend the notion of BGG reciprocity described in [BCM12, BBC+ ] to a more general EMA setting (see [BBC+ , Rem. 2.7]).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let X be an affine scheme of finite type over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero with coordinate ring A, let g be a finite-dimensional target algebra (e.g. a Lie algebra), and let Γ be a finite group acting compatibly on both X (hence on A) and on g by automorphisms. Define the equivariant map algebra
  M = M(X, g)^Γ = (g ⊗ A)^Γ,
the fixed-point subalgebra of g ⊗ A under the diagonal Γ-action.

For such M one has notions of global Weyl module W(λ) and local Weyl module W_loc(λ, ψ), indexed by dominant integral weights λ (for a Cartan subalgebra of the underlying g) and, in the local case, by additional spectral data ψ (e.g. a maximal ideal/point datum of a suitable commutative algebra A_λ acting on W(λ)).

Problem: Develop the theory of global and local Weyl modules for arbitrary equivariant map algebras M(X, g)^Γ, beyond the currently understood cases (which include, for instance, g semisimple with X of finite type and Γ abelian acting freely). In particular:
(a) Determine the length, dimension, and character of the local Weyl modules W_loc(λ, ψ) for general choices of (X, g, Γ).
(b) Formulate and prove a Bernstein–Gelfand–Gelfand (BGG) reciprocity statement in this generality, relating multiplicities of irreducible objects in suitable standard/Weyl filtrations to multiplicities in projective covers within an appropriate category of finite-dimensional M-modules.
artifact.category_tag: Equivariant map algebras and Weyl modules
artifact.status_search_result: Partial progress is documented: global Weyl modules for equivariant map algebras have been defined and studied (Fourier–Manning–Savage, 2013–2015), and local Weyl modules have been analyzed in the case where g is semisimple, X is affine of finite type, and Γ is abelian acting freely. Extensions to equivariant map Lie superalgebras appeared as recently as 2025. However, a complete determination of lengths, dimensions, and characters of local Weyl modules and a general BGG reciprocity for arbitrary equivariant map algebras has not been established, so the broader program remains open.

status_evidence.title: Global Weyl modules for equivariant map algebras
status_evidence.snippet: Defines global Weyl modules for equivariant map algebras under mild assumptions, introduces a Weyl functor, and proves finite generation.
status_evidence.claim: Global Weyl modules have been developed in the EMA setting (partial progress).

status_evidence.title: Local Weyl modules for equivariant map algebras with free abelian group actions
status_evidence.snippet: Extends local Weyl module theory to equivariant map algebras where Γ is abelian and acts freely on X, with g semisimple.
status_evidence.claim: Local Weyl modules known in the abelian free action case, not in full generality.

status_evidence.title: Weyl modules for Equivariant map Lie superalgebras
status_evidence.snippet: Recent extension to the superalgebra setting, indicating the topic is still active.
status_evidence.claim: Research remains ongoing, with extensions to more general settings still appearing.
